_readme: Round 6 of 7 — big august 9th batch (in-copyright PDFs). Synopses grounded in real detect.mjs-extracted text; mentions curated from candidates.json per docs/detector.md exclusion rules; genres per tools/genres.mjs. The Persian Boy backfills a pre-existing metadata-less stub.

books.title: The Naive and the Sentimental Novelist
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: Pamuk's Charles Eliot Norton Lectures at Harvard on what happens in the minds of writers and readers of novels, examining the visual imagination, character, plot, and the elusive 'center' of a novel through his own fiction and classics from Tolstoy to Proust.

books.title: The Nature of Alexander
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: Mary Renault's account of Alexander the Great's life and campaigns, opening with his funeral cortege in Babylon and tracing his conquests through Macedon, Persia, and India using ancient sources such as Arrian, Plutarch, and Diodorus.

books.title: The Orchard Keeper
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.synopsis: Set in a remote Tennessee community between the two world wars, the novel follows the boy John Wesley Rattner, the bootlegger Marion Sylder who unknowingly killed the boy's father, and old Uncle Ather, whose lives converge around an abandoned orchard.

books.title: The Other Americans
books.author: Laila Lalami
books.synopsis: After her father is fatally struck by a hit-and-run driver outside the family's Mojave Desert diner, Nora Guerraoui returns home and, alongside Detective Coleman and her old classmate Jeremy, works through the investigation while confronting her Moroccan immigrant family's history.

books.title: The Pachinko Parlour
books.author: Elisa Shua Dusapin
books.synopsis: A young Franco-Korean woman spends a summer in Tokyo tutoring a Japanese girl named Mieko in French while staying with her aging Korean grandparents, who fled to Japan during the Korean War and never returned, and repeatedly puts off a planned visit to the pachinko parlour they run.

books.title: The Passenger
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.synopsis: A salvage diver in 1980s New Orleans investigates a sunken jet with a passenger missing from the wreckage while his memory of his dead sister, a mathematician who took her own life, keeps intruding as long dialogues with a flippered hallucination called the Thalidomide Kid.

books.title: The Persian Boy
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: A Persian boy named Bagoas, castrated and sold as a slave after his family's ruin, becomes a favorite in King Darius's court and then Alexander the Great's companion, narrating Alexander's conquests and death from inside the royal tent.

books.title: The Praise Singer
books.author: Mary Renault
books.synopsis: The poet Simonides, in old age at the Sicilian court, looks back over his life as a singer trained under the bard Kleobis, his years in tyrant Athens under Pisistratos and his sons, and the murder of Hipparchos by Harmodios and Aristogeiton.

books.title: The Prophet's Hair
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: A relic believed to be a hair from the Prophet Muhammad's beard is stolen in Srinagar and passes through the hands of a moneylender who is transformed into a tyrant, then a professional burglar hired to steal it back, with maiming and ruin following everyone it touches.

books.title: The Red-Haired Woman
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: A teenage apprentice well-digger named Cem, working outside Istanbul under master well-digger Mahmut, falls for an older woman known as the Red-Haired Woman, and a violent accident at the well entangles his life for decades with the myths of Oedipus and of Rostam and Sohrab.

books.title: The Road to San Giovanni
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: Five autobiographical essays in which Calvino reconstructs his father's conviction that their farmland above San Remo was the true world and the town below a mere appendix, revisits his obsessive youth as a moviegoer absorbing 1930s Hollywood stars scene by scene, and recalls his time as a partisan fighter and the mechanics of memory itself.

books.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
books.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
books.synopsis: Magazine writer Monique Grant is summoned by reclusive Hollywood legend Evelyn Hugo to ghostwrite her life story, which Hugo recounts husband by husband, from her escape out of Hell's Kitchen to her decades-long hidden relationship with producer Harry Cameron.

books.title: The Strange Library
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.synopsis: A boy who visits the library to look up how the Ottoman Empire collected taxes is led down into a basement labyrinth where an old man imprisons him to memorize books before eating his brain, and he plots escape with the help of a sheep man and a voiceless girl.

books.title: The Testaments
books.author: Margaret Atwood
books.synopsis: Fifteen years after the events of The Handmaid's Tale, the regime of Gilead is narrated through the interwoven testimonies of Aunt Lydia, who keeps a secret manuscript hidden inside a hollowed-out copy of Cardinal Newman's Apologia Pro Vita Sua in the Ardua Hall archive, and two younger women, Agnes and Daisy, whose paths converge toward the regime's downfall.

books.title: The Three-Body Problem
books.author: Cixin Liu
books.synopsis: Beginning when astrophysicist Ye Wenjie, working at a secret Cultural Revolution-era radio base, makes contact with an alien civilization, the novel follows nanomaterials researcher Wang Miao as he investigates a wave of scientist suicides and the virtual-reality game Three Body, which encodes the plight of the Trisolaran civilization.

books.title: The Uses of Literature
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: A collection of Calvino's essays and lectures, spanning theoretical pieces on cybernetics, structuralism, and "levels of reality" in fiction alongside close readings of specific classics — the Odyssey, Ovid's Metamorphoses, Ariosto's Orlando Furioso, Stendhal's Charterhouse of Parma, Manzoni's The Betrothed, Balzac's city fiction, Voltaire's Candide, and Cyrano de Bergerac's lunar fantasy — plus shorter pieces on Fourier, Marianne Moore, Pliny, and Roland Barthes.

books.title: The White Castle
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.synopsis: A frame narrative presents a manuscript found by a modern editor: the first-person account of a young Italian scholar captured by pirates and enslaved in seventeenth-century Istanbul, given as a gift to "Hoja," an Ottoman scholar who so physically resembles him that the two become entangled in an obsessive intellectual and psychological rivalry. Together they serve the sultan as astrologers/scientists and design a giant siege weapon used in a military campaign against a fortress, while their identities increasingly blur and swap.

books.title: The Dream Hotel
books.author: Laila Lalami
books.synopsis: In a near-future America, Sara Hussein is held at "Madison," a retention center (a converted elementary school run by private contractor Safe-X) after being flagged by a predictive-policing "risk score" system tied to a neural implant called the Dreamsaver that monitors her dreams; the book follows her daily life among fellow retainees and her strained correspondence with her husband and children, as she and others push back against the facility's surveillance and precrime detention regime.

books.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
books.author: Gabrielle Zevin
books.synopsis: In late-1990s/2000s Cambridge and Los Angeles, childhood acquaintances Sam Masur and Sadie Green reunite as young adults and, together with Sam's roommate Marx, found a video game studio, building acclaimed titles while navigating Sam's chronic pain from a foot injury/amputation, professional rivalry, and a decades-long entangled friendship.

books.title: Truman
books.author: David McCullough
books.synopsis: This biography of Harry S. Truman covers his boyhood and youth in Independence, Missouri, his World War I artillery service in France, his rise through Kansas City's Pendergast political machine, his vice presidency and accession to the presidency on Roosevelt's death, and his presidency through the atomic bomb decision, the Marshall Plan, the 1948 campaign, the Korean War and firing of MacArthur, into his retirement in Independence and death, drawing on his diaries, letters, and interviews with associates.

books.title: Under the Jaguar Sun
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: Three linked stories, left unfinished at Calvino's death, meant to explore the five senses: a couple touring Oaxaca's convents and ruins whose relationship becomes entangled with the region's cuisine and colonial history; a deposed king reduced to paranoid listening from his throne room; and a man obsessed with tracking a lost lover through scent alone.

books.title: Victory City
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.synopsis: A blind poet-prophetess, Pampa Kampana, lives two hundred and forty-seven years and narrates the rise and fall of the empire of Bisnaga, which she conjures from a handful of magic seeds and populates by whispering invented life stories into her subjects' ears, spanning generations of kings, wars, and dynastic betrayal.

books.title: Walking with the Comrades
books.author: Arundhati Roy
books.synopsis: Reportage essays from Roy's weeks traveling with Maoist guerrillas in the forests of central India, describing the Janatana Sarkar's armed cadres, women commanders like Comrade Niti who carries an AK on her shoulder, and the war between the Indian state and adivasi insurgents in Chhattisgarh's Dandakaranya region.

books.title: Water for Elephants
books.author: Sara Gruen
books.synopsis: An elderly Jacob Jankowski recalls his youth as a veterinary student who joins the Benzini Brothers traveling circus during the Great Depression, working the menagerie under the volatile boss August, falling for August's wife Marlena, and caring for the elephant Rosie amid the show's harsh, itinerant world.

books.title: When She Was Good
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: In the small Midwestern town of Liberty Center, Lucy Nelson grows up hardened by her father's alcoholism and her family's failures, setting her will against them and later against her husband Roy Bassart, whom she marries despite secretly despising him.
